chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you intend to bow, say while standing: Allahu Akbar, then bow and say: 'My Lord, to You I have bowed, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, and upon You I have relied. You are my Lord. My hearing, my sight, my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my marrow, my nerves, my bones, and what my feet carry have humbled to You, not being arrogant, nor haughty, nor regretful. Glory is to my Lord, the Magnificent, and to Him be praise,' three times with ease. And arrange your feet in your bowing, placing between them a span's width. Press your palms against your knees. Place your right hand on your right knee before the left. Press the tips of your fingers against the knee joint itself. Spread your fingers when you place them on your knees. Keep your back straight, extend your neck, and let your gaze be between your feet.

Then say: 'Allah heard him who praised Him,' while you are standing upright: 'All praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds,' those of dominion and majesty and greatness, 'All praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds,' you proclaim it with your voice. Then raise your hands with the Takbir and fall prostrating.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: All praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds
key_terms.سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ: Allah heard him who praised Him (recited upon rising)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: Glory to my Lord, the Magnificent (recited in ruku')

ai.seo_question: What are the specific physical postures and recitations prescribed for the bowing (ruku') in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a detailed jurisprudential guide for the physical postures and recitations of Ruku' and I'tidal, emphasizing the integration of bodily humility with spiritual submission. It highlights the Shia emphasis on precise bodily alignment—such as placing the right hand on the right knee before the left—as a manifestation of *khushu'* (devotion), linking physical discipline to the recitation of divine attributes. The instruction to recite 'Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim' three times reflects the Prophetic tradition of maintaining consistency in dhikr during prayer, reinforcing the connection between the body and the soul in worship.
